title: How Does a Zipper Actually Work?
summary: Two rows of teeth and one little slider: here is the clever trick that holds every zipper together.

beats.text: You zip something up every day without thinking. But how does a zipper actually hold together?
Look closely: a zipper is just two rows of tiny teeth and one little slider.
Quick guess. What locks the teeth together?
beats.reveal: Tiny hooks! Each tooth has a bump on top and a hollow underneath.

beats.text: As the slider moves up, it pushes the two rows together at an angle. Each bump drops into the hollow above it.
Bump into hollow, bump into hollow, all the way up. Together they hold like a tiny chain.
Unzipping? Inside the slider sits a small wedge. It pries the teeth apart, one pair at a time.
Bonus tip: if your zipper splits open behind the slider, the slider has usually worn loose. A gentle squeeze with pliers can fix it.

visual.text: A zipper that splits behind the slider usually has a worn, loose slider.
